chapter: Brown's Band in Chicago and New York
title: Tommy Brown's band and its jobs
summary: Before leaving he played guitar in Tommy Brown's band, which took work from Laine and played parks and across the river.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah, before you left there? Oh, well, I was working with Tommy Brown then. Uh, Tommy Brown in a regular outfit. Yeah, I was playing guitar with him. Uh, huh. You see? They had, uh, Gus Miller on clarinet, Raymond Lopez on trumpet, Tommy Brown on trombone, Bill Lambert on drums, and Steve Brown on bass, and myself on guitar. That was a band. Well, those days, Tommy had cut deeply into Jack Lane, uh, as far as work is concerned. We had quite a bit of work, and we got more money that, uh, Tommy Brown than we did with Jack. Mm-hmm. For the same number of hours. Mm-hmm. But as you know,
a dollar and a half all day long at Millenburg or West End. What about baseball games? You all played out the Ironman Park?
Well, I can't quite remember vividly whether we did or not. I suppose we did, because we played everything around here and across the river, Metry and all in there. We played at, uh, what's the name

of that park in Metry? Uh, it begins with an E, I think. It's no longer there. Oh, is that Lecter Park? No, it's another one. Right over there, uh, Eastman? Eastman. Yeah. You played there? Oh, yes. We played all that. Sometime or rather we played all around. Did you all ever play any of the pretendy dances at Tulane?
